recent_posts.title: Building Blocks for AI Part 3
recent_posts.summary: The Microsoft Agent Framework (1.0 release, April 2026) is a .NET SDK for building intelligent AI agents. Built on top of IChatClient from Microsoft Extensions for AI, it enables agents that can use tools, maintain multi-turn conversation sessions, persist memory across sessions via AIContextProvider, and coordinate in graph-based workflows. Key patterns covered include: creating agents with AsAIAgent(), equipping them with tools via AIFunctionFactory, managing conversation state with AgentSession (including serialization), building cross-session memory, and orchestrating multi-agent workflows (sequential, concurrent, conditional routing, writer-critic feedback loops, and sub-workflows). Human-in-the-loop approval for sensitive tool calls is also supported. The framework integrates naturally with VectorData for RAG patterns and will be followed by a post on Model Context Protocol (MCP).

recent_posts.title: Governing MCP tool calls in .NET with the Agent Governance Toolkit
recent_posts.summary: The Agent Governance Toolkit (AGT) provides a .NET governance layer for MCP tool calls in AI agent systems. It includes McpSecurityScanner for detecting malicious tool definitions (e.g., prompt injection, typosquatting), McpResponseSanitizer for cleaning tool outputs, McpGateway for policy-based access control, and GovernanceKernel for wiring everything together with YAML policies, audit events, and OpenTelemetry. The toolkit maps to the OWASP MCP Top 10 risks and requires no external services. Install via the Microsoft.AgentGovernance NuGet package targeting .NET 8.0+.

recent_posts.title: Combining API versioning with OpenAPI in .NET 10 applications
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to implementing API versioning in .NET 10 applications using the new Asp.Versioning v10 package alongside Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi. Covers both controllers and Minimal APIs, explains versioning strategies (URL, query string, header), and shows how to generate separate OpenAPI documents per version using the new WithDocumentPerVersion() method. Also demonstrates integrating SwaggerUI and Scalar for visualizing versioned API docs, compares the v8 vs v10 setup to highlight reduced boilerplate, and briefly covers API linting with Spectral and oasdiff.

recent_posts.title: ASP.NET Core 2.3 end of support announcement
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft has announced that ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach end of support on April 7, 2027, providing the required 12 months advance notice. After that date, no security patches, bug fixes, or technical support will be provided. Existing applications will continue to run, but will be exposed to unpatched security vulnerabilities. Microsoft recommends upgrading to a currently supported version such as .NET 10 (LTS) and suggests using GitHub Copilot App Modernization to assist with the migration process.

recent_posts.title: Generative AI for Beginners .NET: Version 2 on .NET 10
recent_posts.summary: Version 2 of the free open-source course 'Generative AI for Beginners .NET' has been released, completely rebuilt on .NET 10. The curriculum is restructured into five focused lessons covering generative AI fundamentals, practical techniques (chat completions, prompt engineering, RAG, function calling), AI application patterns, multi-agent systems using the Microsoft Agent Framework, and responsible AI. The primary AI abstraction has shifted from Semantic Kernel to Microsoft.Extensions.AI (MEAI), which aligns with .NET 10 patterns like dependency injection. RAG samples have been rewritten using native SDKs, 11 legacy Semantic Kernel samples moved to deprecated, and all eight language translations updated.

recent_posts.title: Pin Clustering in .NET MAUI Maps
recent_posts.summary: NET MAUI 11 Preview 2 introduces pin clustering for the Map control on Android and iOS/Mac Catalyst. A single property `IsClusteringEnabled="True"` activates automatic grouping of nearby pins into cluster markers with count badges. Pins can be assigned a `ClusteringIdentifier` to form independent clusters by category (e.g., coffee shops vs. parks). A `ClusterClicked` event provides access to the pins in a cluster, their geographic center, and the ability to suppress default zoom behavior. On Android, a custom grid-based algorithm handles clustering; on iOS/Mac Catalyst, native MapKit `MKClusterAnnotation` support is used. The feature is available in .NET 11 Preview 2 with sample code in the maui-samples repository.

recent_posts.title: Modernize .NET Anywhere with GitHub Copilot
recent_posts.summary: The modernize-dotnet custom agent extends GitHub Copilot's .NET modernization workflow beyond Visual Studio to VS Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, and GitHub itself. The agent follows an assess → plan → execute model, generating three artifacts per run: an assessment, an upgrade plan, and upgrade tasks stored alongside the code for team review. Supported workloads include ASP.NET Core, Blazor, Azure Functions, WPF, class libraries, and console apps, plus .NET Framework migrations. Organizations can also define custom skills to encode internal migration patterns into the workflow.

recent_posts.title: Release v1.0 of the official MCP C# SDK
recent_posts.summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) C# SDK has reached v1.0, implementing the 2025-11-25 MCP Specification. Key additions include: enhanced OAuth authorization server discovery with three PRM exposure methods; icon metadata for tools, resources, and prompts; incremental scope consent following the principle of least privilege; URL mode elicitation for secure out-of-band user interactions; tool calling support within LLM sampling requests using Microsoft.Extensions.AI; OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) as a preferred alternative to Dynamic Client Registration; long-running HTTP request handling via SSE polling with DistributedCacheEventStreamStore; and experimental Tasks support for durable state tracking and deferred result retrieval with lifecycle management.

recent_posts.title: GitHub Copilot Testing for .NET Brings AI-powered Unit Tests to Visual Studio 2026
recent_posts.summary: GitHub Copilot Testing for .NET is now generally available in Visual Studio 2026 v18.3, offering AI-powered unit test generation with automatic build, execution, and failure recovery. The release introduces free-form natural language prompting (using @Test), multiple entry points including right-click context menus and chat icebreakers, and support for generating tests at various scopes from single members to entire solutions. The agent automatically creates test projects, organizes tests according to your framework preferences, and provides coverage summaries with pass/fail insights.

recent_posts.title: .NET Framework 3.5 Moves to Standalone Deployment in new versions of Windows
recent_posts.summary: .NET Framework 3.5 will no longer be included as an optional Windows component starting with Windows 11 Insider Preview Build 27965. Instead, it must be installed via a standalone installer for legacy applications. This change affects future Windows releases but not Windows 10 or Windows 11 through 25H2. The shift aligns with .NET Framework 3.5's approaching end of support on January 9, 2029, and Microsoft encourages migration to newer .NET versions. Detailed guidance, installers, and migration paths are available on Microsoft Learn.
